**Who Can Take Part?**

The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 is open to all children and young people who are residents of the Greater Bendigo region, as well as visitors who are staying in the area for at least part of the school summer holidays. We welcome readers from all backgrounds and abilities, and participation is completely free.

There are four age groups for the challenge:

- **Little Readers** – for children aged 0–5 years. This group is designed for parents, grandparents, and carers to share books, rhymes, and stories with their little ones. Babies and toddlers can be registered by an adult, and every book or rhyme session shared together counts towards the challenge.
- **Junior Readers** – for children aged 6–9 years. Junior Readers can read books, graphic novels, or listen to audiobooks. We encourage them to explore different genres and try something new – whether that is a picture book, a chapter book, or a non-fiction title about dinosaurs, space, or animals.
- **Independent Readers** – for children aged 10–12 years. This group is for readers who are ready to tackle longer chapter books, series, or non-fiction. We encourage Independent Readers to set their own reading goals and to challenge themselves with books that are slightly above their usual reading level, if they feel comfortable doing so.
- **Teen Readers** – for young people aged 13–17 years. Teen Readers can choose from young adult fiction, graphic novels, manga, non-fiction, or any other reading material that interests them. Audiobooks and e-books also count for this age group.

Please note that age groups are based on the child's age as at the start of the challenge in January 2025. If your child turns six, ten, or thirteen during the challenge period, they remain in the age group they started in. This keeps the competition fair and simple for families with more than one child.

**How to Register**

Registration is easy and can be done in three ways:

1. **In person** – visit any of our library branches across the Greater Bendigo region, including Bendigo Library, Eaglehawk Library, Heathcote Library, Kangaroo Flat Library, Castlemaine Library (service level agreement), and our mobile library stops. Staff will help you register on the spot and give you a reading log booklet.
2. **Online** – complete the registration form on our website. You will need to provide your child's name, date of birth, and your contact details. Once registered online, you can collect your reading log booklet from your chosen branch, or you can download a printable version from the website.
3. **By phone** – call the library on 1300 362 322 during opening hours and a staff member will register your child over the phone. Please have your child's details ready.

Each child needs their own registration, even if they are in the same family. This helps us track individual progress and ensures that every child receives their own prizes and certificates at the end of the challenge.

**What You Need to Do**

The challenge is simple: read as much as you can during the summer holidays. For every book, audiobook, or e-book your child finishes, record it in the reading log. For Little Readers, a shared storytime session or a picture book read together counts as one entry.

- Junior Readers are encouraged to read at least 12 books over the course of the challenge. This works out to roughly one book every few days, which is achievable for most readers.
- Independent Readers are encouraged to read at least 8 books. Because these books are often longer, we have set a slightly lower target to allow for deeper reading.
- Teen Readers are encouraged to read at least 6 books. We know that teenagers have busy schedules with school, sport, and social activities, so we have kept the target flexible.
- Little Readers are encouraged to record at least 20 shared reading sessions. This could be the same book read ten times – repetition is wonderful for early literacy!

**How to Record Your Reading**

Your reading log booklet is your passport to prizes, so keep it somewhere safe – perhaps on the fridge or in the family book basket. Every time your child finishes a book, audiobook, or e-book, write it down. For Little Readers, every shared storytime session or picture book read together counts as one entry, so don't be shy about recording the same favourite book more than once. Repetition is a powerful part of early literacy, and we want to celebrate it.

**Step-by-step guide to filling in your reading log:**

1. **Write the title** of the book in the space provided. If your child has read a book in a language other than English, that is wonderful – please write the title in the original language and, if you like, add the English translation in brackets.
2. **Write the author's name** if you know it. If not, just leave it blank; we don't want the logging to become a chore.
3. **Tick the format box** – book, audiobook, or e-book. For Little Readers, tick the "shared reading" box instead.
4. **Add the date** your child finished the book. This is just for your own record and to help us see the reading momentum across the region.
5. **Initial or sign** each entry once it is complete. This is a small step that helps children feel a sense of accomplishment as they see their log fill up.

That's it. There is no need to write a review or answer questions about the book. We know that some children love to talk about what they have read, and some prefer to keep it private – both are perfectly fine. The log is a record, not a test.

**Tips for Parents and Guardians**

We have put together a few suggestions to help your child get the most out of the Summer Reading Challenge. These are not rules – just ideas that have worked well for other families in previous years.

- **Set a regular reading time.** Whether it is ten minutes before bed, or half an hour after lunch when the house is quiet, a consistent time helps reading become a habit. The summer holidays can be unstructured, so a little routine goes a long way.
- **Let your child choose.** Children are far more likely to read – and to finish – books that they have picked out themselves. Even if the choice seems too easy or too hard, let them try. Our librarians are happy to make suggestions, but the final choice should always be the child's.
- **Mix it up.** Audiobooks count, and they are great for long car trips or quiet time after swimming. E-books are also welcome. You can borrow e-books free from our library using the Libby app – just ask staff if you need help setting it up.
- **Read aloud together.** For Junior and Independent Readers, you might still enjoy reading a chapter aloud together at night. This counts as reading, of course. Many parents tell us that their older children still love being read to, even when they can read perfectly well themselves.
- **For Little Readers, follow their lead.** If your toddler wants to read the same board book five times in a row, that is five entries in the log. If they only sit still for two pages of a longer picture book, that still counts as a shared reading session. The goal is to build positive associations with books, not to enforce a set number of pages.
- **Keep the log visible.** Children love to see their progress. You might like to count the entries together at the end of each week and talk about how many more books they need to reach their target. Some families like to put a sticker on each entry; others prefer to just tick. Whatever works for your family is the right approach.
- **Don't stress about lost books.** If you lose the reading log booklet, come in to any branch and we will give you a replacement. We will also have spare booklets at all the challenge celebration events, so you can pick one up there. If you registered online, you can always print another copy from the website. There is no need to start again – just transfer the entries you remember, or start fresh if you prefer. The important thing is to keep reading, not to keep paperwork.

When you register, you will receive a welcome pack containing your child's reading log, a sticker sheet, and a guide to the challenge. The reading log is used to track the books your child reads over the summer.

**3. Do we need to read a certain number of books?**

The challenge is designed to be flexible and encouraging rather than prescriptive. We ask that children aim to read at least 12 books over the summer period. However, we understand that every child is different – some may read more, some may read fewer, and some may prefer to listen to audiobooks or read ebooks. What matters most is that children are enjoying reading and building their confidence.

For younger children (aged 5 to 7), we encourage parents and carers to read aloud with them. Books that are read to a child by an adult or older sibling count towards the challenge, as do audiobooks and ebooks.

**4. What counts as a "book"?**

Almost anything! Picture books, chapter books, graphic novels, non-fiction, audiobooks, and ebooks all count. We even count magazines and comics if your child reads them from cover to cover. The goal is to get children excited about reading in whatever format works for them.

**5. How do I record the books my child reads?**

Each child has their own reading log, which is a simple booklet with space to record the title and author of each book they finish. You can also use the online reading log on our website if you prefer – simply log in with the details provided in your welcome pack and add books as you go.

We recommend updating the log as you go rather than trying to remember everything at the end. It only takes a minute to jot down a title, and it's a lovely way to look back at all the reading your child has done.

**Summer Reading Challenge 2025 – Program Announcement and Key Dates**

**Who Can Take Part?**

The Summer Reading Challenge 2025 is open to all children and young people who are residents of the Greater Bendigo region, as well as visitors who are staying in the area for at least part of the school summer holidays. We welcome readers from all backgrounds and abilities, and participation is completely free.

There are four age groups for the challenge:

- **Little Readers** – for children aged 0–5 years. This group is designed for parents, grandparents, and carers to share books, rhymes, and stories with their little ones. Babies and toddlers can be registered by an adult, and every book or rhyme session shared together counts towards the challenge.
- **Junior Readers** – for children aged 6–9 years. Junior Readers can read books, graphic novels, or listen to audiobooks. We encourage them to explore different genres and try something new – whether that is a picture book, a chapter book, or a non-fiction title about dinosaurs, space, or animals.
- **Independent Readers** – for children aged 10–12 years. This group is for readers who are ready to tackle longer chapter books, series, or non-fiction. We encourage Independent Readers to set their own reading goals and to challenge themselves with books that are slightly above their usual reading level, if they feel comfortable doing so.
- **Teen Readers** – for young people aged 13–17 years. Teen Readers can choose from young adult fiction, graphic novels, manga, non-fiction, or any other reading material that interests them. Audiobooks and e-books also count for this age group.

Please note that age groups are based on the child's age as at the start of the challenge in January 2025. If your child turns six, ten, or thirteen during the challenge period, they remain in the age group they started in. This keeps the competition fair and simple for families with more than one child.

**How to Register**

Registration is easy and can be done in three ways:

1. **In person** – visit any of our library branches across the Greater Bendigo region, including Bendigo Library, Eaglehawk Library, Heathcote Library, Kangaroo Flat Library, Castlemaine Library (service level agreement), and our mobile library stops. Staff will help you register on the spot and give you a reading log booklet.
2. **Online** – complete the registration form on our website. You will need to provide your child's name, date of birth, and your contact details. Once registered online, you can collect your reading log booklet from your chosen branch, or you can download a printable version from the website.
3. **By phone** – call the library on 1300 362 322 during opening hours and a staff member will register your child over the phone. Please have your child's details ready.

Each child needs their own registration, even if they are in the same family. This helps us track individual progress and ensures that every child receives their own prizes and certificates at the end of the challenge.

**What You Need to Do**

The challenge is simple: read as much as you can during the summer holidays. For every book, audiobook, or e-book your child finishes, record it in the reading log. For Little Readers, a shared storytime session or a picture book read together counts as one entry.

- Junior Readers are encouraged to read at least 12 books over the course of the challenge. This works out to roughly one book every few days, which is achievable for most readers.
- Independent Readers are encouraged to read at least 8 books. Because these books are often longer, we have set a slightly lower target to allow for deeper reading.
- Teen Readers are encouraged to read at least 6 books. We know that teenagers have busy schedules with school, sport, and social activities, so we have kept the target flexible.
- Little Readers are encouraged to record at least 20 shared reading sessions. This could be the same book read ten times – repetition is wonderful for early literacy!

**How to Record Your Reading**

Your reading log booklet is your passport to prizes, so keep it somewhere safe – perhaps on the fridge or in the family book basket. Every time your child finishes a book, audiobook, or e-book, write it down. For Little Readers, every shared storytime session or picture book read together counts as one entry, so don't be shy about recording the same favourite book more than once. Repetition is a powerful part of early literacy, and we want to celebrate it.

**Step-by-step guide to filling in your reading log:**

1. **Write the title** of the book in the space provided. If your child has read a book in a language other than English, that is wonderful – please write the title in the original language and, if you like, add the English translation in brackets.
2. **Write the author's name** if you know it. If not, just leave it blank; we don't want the logging to become a chore.
3. **Tick the format box** – book, audiobook, or e-book. For Little Readers, tick the "shared reading" box instead.
4. **Add the date** your child finished the book. This is just for your own record and to help us see the reading momentum across the region.
5. **Initial or sign** each entry once it is complete. This is a small step that helps children feel a sense of accomplishment as they see their log fill up.

That's it. There is no need to write a review or answer questions about the book. We know that some children love to talk about what they have read, and some prefer to keep it private – both are perfectly fine. The log is a record, not a test.

**Tips for Parents and Guardians**

We have put together a few suggestions to help your child get the most out of the Summer Reading Challenge. These are not rules – just ideas that have worked well for other families in previous years.

- **Set a regular reading time.** Whether it is ten minutes before bed, or half an hour after lunch when the house is quiet, a consistent time helps reading become a habit. The summer holidays can be unstructured, so a little routine goes a long way.
- **Let your child choose.** Children are far more likely to read – and to finish – books that they have picked out themselves. Even if the choice seems too easy or too hard, let them try. Our librarians are happy to make suggestions, but the final choice should always be the child's.
- **Mix it up.** Audiobooks count, and they are great for long car trips or quiet time after swimming. E-books are also welcome. You can borrow e-books free from our library using the Libby app – just ask staff if you need help setting it up.
- **Read aloud together.** For Junior and Independent Readers, you might still enjoy reading a chapter aloud together at night. This counts as reading, of course. Many parents tell us that their older children still love being read to, even when they can read perfectly well themselves.
- **For Little Readers, follow their lead.** If your toddler wants to read the same board book five times in a row, that is five entries in the log. If they only sit still for two pages of a longer picture book, that still counts as a shared reading session. The goal is to build positive associations with books, not to enforce a set number of pages.
- **Keep the log visible.** Children love to see their progress. You might like to count the entries together at the end of each week and talk about how many more books they need to reach their target. Some families like to put a sticker on each entry; others prefer to just tick. Whatever works for your family is the right approach.
- **Don't stress about lost books.** If you lose the reading log booklet, come in to any branch and we will give you a replacement. We will also have spare booklets at all the challenge celebration events, so you can pick one up there. If you registered online, you can always print another copy from the website. There is no need to start again – just transfer the entries you remember, or start fresh if you prefer. The important thing is to keep reading, not to keep paperwork.

**After hours:** If you have a question about the challenge outside of office hours, please email us. We check our inbox regularly and will respond as soon as we can.

**Frequently Asked Questions**

**1. Who can take part in the Summer Reading Challenge?**

The challenge is open to all children aged 5 to 12 years who are residents of the Greater Bendigo region. Children do not need to be members of the library to participate, but we do encourage families to sign up for a free library membership while they are visiting – it takes just a few minutes and gives you access to thousands of books, ebooks, audiobooks, and more.

**2. How do I register my child?**

Registration is easy. You can:

- Visit any of our branches (Bendigo, Eaglehawk, Kangaroo Flat, or Heathcote) and speak to a staff member.
- Register online via our website at www.bendigolibrary.vic.gov.au/summerreading.
- Call us on (03) 5449 2790 during office hours.

When you register, you will receive a welcome pack containing your child's reading log, a sticker sheet, and a guide to the challenge. The reading log is used to track the books your child reads over the summer.

**3. Do we need to read a certain number of books?**

The challenge is designed to be flexible and encouraging rather than prescriptive. We ask that children aim to read at least 12 books over the summer period. However, we understand that every child is different – some may read more, some may read fewer, and some may prefer to listen to audiobooks or read ebooks. What matters most is that children are enjoying reading and building their confidence.

For younger children (aged 5 to 7), we encourage parents and carers to read aloud with them. Books that are read to a child by an adult or older sibling count towards the challenge, as do audiobooks and ebooks.

**4. What counts as a "book"?**

Almost anything! Picture books, chapter books, graphic novels, non-fiction, audiobooks, and ebooks all count. We even count magazines and comics if your child reads them from cover to cover. The goal is to get children excited about reading in whatever format works for them.

**5. How do I record the books my child reads?**

Each child has their own reading log, which is a simple booklet with space to record the title and author of each book they finish. You can also use the online reading log on our website if you prefer – simply log in with the details provided in your welcome pack and add books as you go.

We recommend updating the log as you go rather than trying to remember everything at the end. It only takes a minute to jot down a title, and it's a lovely way to look back at all the reading your child has done.
